question: What is the primary goal of the Drug Revolving Fund model in hospitals?

options.A: To provide free medical care for all citizens
options.B: To maintain a steady stock of essential medicines
options.C: To generate heavy profits for private investors
options.D: To reduce the number of employed pharmacy staff

explanation: The fund ensures continuous drug availability by using money from sales to buy new stock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why do strict cash-and-carry drug schemes create problems for vulnerable patients?

options.A: Doctors refuse to write prescriptions for cash buyers
options.B: Patients without immediate cash are denied essential drugs
options.C: Pharmacies end up with too much physical inventory
options.D: Drug manufacturers stop supplying generic medications

explanation: Requiring upfront payment for every single medication blocks access for those living in extreme poverty. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h1)

question: The main purpose of a DRF exemption is to protect whom?

options.A: Pharmaceutical suppliers from delayed government payments
options.B: Hospital management from financial audit queries
options.C: Vulnerable populations from catastrophic health spending

explanation: Exemptions shield poor patients from spending their entire livelihood on sudden medical crises. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h2)

question: How do exemptions affect the operational balance of a revolving drug fund?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for patient drug sales
options.B: They shorten the shelf life of stored pharmaceutical products
options.C: They increase the profit margins on non-exempt medications
options.D: They require external subsidies to replace uncollected cash

explanation: Since free drugs break the cash cycle, outside funding must cover those costs to keep the fund alive. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which group is typically included among patients eligible for DRF exemptions?

options.B: Children under five years of age

explanation: Under-five children belong to vulnerable demographics often protected by public health exemption policies. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why are emergency trauma victims given immediate drug exemptions before financial checks?

options.A: Hospital accountants prefer processing paperwork later
options.B: Delaying treatment for payment verification can cause death
options.C: Trauma patients never have bank accounts or cash
options.D: Emergency drugs are always free to manufacture

explanation: In acute emergencies, saving life takes absolute precedence over administrative billing processes. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h3)

question: What type of clinical condition is most likely to qualify for an immediate DRF exemption?
explanation: Obstetric emergencies directly threaten maternal and child survival, making them priority targets for exemptions. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why are epidemic diseases included in free drug exemption lists?

options.A: To reduce the workload of private community pharmacists
options.B: To test new pharmaceutical products on infected populations
options.C: To prevent community transmission and control outbreaks fast
options.D: To increase international travel restrictions on citizens

explanation: Treating infectious outbreaks quickly stops the spread and protects the wider public health. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h4)

question: What happens to a drug revolving fund if exemptions are given without external subsidies?

options.A: The hospital generates higher profits from remaining drugs
options.B: Patients begin donating their own medicines to the ward
options.C: The fund experiences stock depletion and eventual collapse
options.D: Pharmaceutical companies lower their global manufacturing prices

explanation: Giving away drugs without replacing the money drains the inventory until no stock is left. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h5)

question: How do government subventions protect a revolving drug fund during patient exemptions?

options.A: They force drug manufacturers to produce medicines at zero cost
options.B: They pay the salaries of hospital security guards and cleaners
options.C: They audit the financial records of private medical stores
options.D: They reimburse the pharmacy for the cost of dispensed free drugs

explanation: Government funds replace the cash value of free medications so the pharmacy can restock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which professional is primarily responsible for assessing the socioeconomic status of indigent patients?
explanation: Social workers are trained to evaluate household income and verify claims of extreme poverty. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do emergency drug waivers use a retrospective review process?

options.A: To calculate the exact profit margin for the pharmacy
options.B: To punish doctors who order unapproved medications
options.C: To confirm eligibility details after saving the patient's life
options.D: To delay the restocking of emergency trauma trays

explanation: Retrospective review allows rapid life-saving treatment while ensuring administrative rules are met afterward. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h6)

question: A major operational challenge for DRF exemptions in public facilities is:

options.A: An oversupply of trained medical social workers
options.B: Excessive profits generated by hospital pharmacies
options.C: Delayed government disbursements of subsidy funds
options.D: Too many patients paying their bills on time

explanation: When promised subsidies take too long to arrive, the drug revolving chain stalls completely. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is the consequence of poor record-keeping in managing drug exemptions?

options.A: Faster processing times for medical social work assessments
options.B: Automatic approval of all emergency surgical procedures
options.C: Lower prices charged by external pharmaceutical vendors
options.D: Stock discrepancies and friction between finance and clinical staff

explanation: Unrecorded free issues create missing inventory gaps that spark conflict during financial audits. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding DRF exemptions at the ward level?

options.A: Manufacturing essential intravenous fluids in the laboratory
options.B: Identifying vulnerable patients who qualify for emergency waivers
options.C: Auditing the annual balance sheets of the hospital pharmacy
options.D: Setting the retail prices for all revolving fund medicines

explanation: Nurses spend the most time at the bedside and spot patients who need immediate exemption support. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h8)

question: How does nurse advocacy improve care for patients requiring drug exemptions?

options.A: By replacing medical social workers during evening shifts
options.B: By providing personal loans to patients from private accounts
options.C: By rewriting hospital financial policies without board approval
options.D: By clearing administrative bottlenecks between the ward and pharmacy

explanation: Nurses push paperwork through quickly so patients get their medications without unnecessary delays. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h8)
